claims.value: Jourdan gives side A 18 battalions estimated by Marchand at 9,000 infantry, four cavalry regiments with 800 horses, and 18 guns.
claims.rationale: Mediated own-report population, not an independently inspected original return. English rendering (ours): "His corps comprised eighteen battalions, which he estimated at only nine thousand men, four cavalry regiments with only eight hundred horses, and eighteen guns."

claims.value: Toreno gives side A 10,000 infantry and 1,200 cavalry arriving before the Spanish position on 18 October.
claims.rationale: Opponent alternative retained, including differing gun count; not averaged with Marchand’s estimate. English rendering (ours): "Marchand, reinforced and bringing ten thousand infantry, twelve hundred cavalry and fourteen guns, appeared before the Spanish position on 18 October."

claims.value: Jourdan says reports described side B as 25,000–30,000 before the battle; their arrival at Madrid was delayed until 21 October.
claims.rationale: Explicit reported estimate, not a dated own Spanish local return. English rendering (ours): "His army was said to be twenty-five to thirty thousand strong."

claims.value: Marchand’s report as transmitted by Jourdan assigns Maucune the main attack and Marcognet the centre.
claims.rationale: The same page assigns Maucune the principal attack; transmission is within Jourdan’s family, not an independent review/report family. English rendering (ours): "Marcognet was assigned the central attack."

claims.value: Toreno describes del Parque intervening at the threatened point with his second Mendizabal.
claims.rationale: Interested account of local intervention, not a readiness measure. English rendering (ours): "Del Parque came to the danger and addressed the troops; his second Mendizabal dismounted and held the soldiers."
